subject: GPU failover checklist and customer update — Acme Analytics impact
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: GPU failover anomaly affecting dedicated pool (Acme)

Hi Lydia — I’m Diego from Redwood Inference ops. We detected an autoscaler hang in the us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool that your account is using. Between 07:43 and 08:02 PDT this morning a subset of requests to your reserved nodes experienced elevated tail latency and a small number of 500s.

Quick facts: 
- Impact window: ~07:43–08:02 PDT
- Symptom: autoscaler process stalled during a kernel rollout; some nodes did not transition to expected ready state
- Customers affected: small fraction of Dedicated customers in us-west-2 (we have scoped to your reserved pool)

We’re attaching a short incident snapshot with timestamps and error traces (incident_snapshot_20270410.log). Our on-call is taking action now — immediate steps are: rollback the kernel change to the last known-good image, restart the autoscaler, and shift traffic for short-lived sessions to warm pools while we validate.

I’ll keep this thread for customer comms and cc our internal ops leads. I’ll follow up with a brief checklist of what we’ve done and next steps in ~30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we know latency spikes are unacceptable.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_snapshot_20270410.log (text)
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: GPU failover anomaly affecting dedicated pool (Acme)

Thanks Diego — we’re seeing the same. Our telemetry shows a spike in 99th pct latency from 07:45–07:59 and ~0.8% request failures for the pipeline that hits your dedicated pool. We’ve attached our request IDs to the ticket (ops@acmeanalytics.com).

We need two things: 1) confirmation when traffic is routed back to our reserved nodes and 2) a preliminary credit for measurable downtime/failed requests — we’ll collect exact numbers on our side.

Lydia
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:28:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: GPU failover anomaly affecting dedicated pool (Acme)

Team — forwarding Acme’s notes. They reported tail latency and ~0.8% failures. Key asks: confirm when traffic is back, and provide a credit estimate.

Immediate ops checklist (please reply inline with status):
- [ ] Rollback kernel rollout to image v20270328 (suspected trigger)
- [ ] Restart autoscaler service for us-west-2 dedicated cluster A
- [ ] Shift short-lived sessions for Acme to warm pools to avoid retries impacting SLA
- [ ] Collect node-level traces and attach to INC-20270410 (link below)
- [ ] Prepare customer-friendly one-paragraph update and proposed credit (10% or to-be-adjusted)

I’ve attached the snapshot I sent Lydia. If rollback is needed we should coordinate minimal-impact window. Also advise if we should proactively move other similar tenants off the affected rolling update.

Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:39:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: GPU failover anomaly affecting dedicated pool (Acme)

On it — status update:
- Rollback: initiating rollback to v20270328 on us-west-2 dedicated cluster A (start 08:41 PDT). Rolling back the kernel change that was in the 02:00 rollout window.
- Autoscaler: will restart after rollback completes; prepping a quick health probe to validate readiness before we bring autoscaler back online.
- Traffic shift: engineering will shift Acme traffic to warm pools (low-latency warm nodes) for ~15 minutes while we validate readiness.
- Traces: collecting node-level traces; uploading to INC-20270410 with a short summary.

I’m attaching the patch diff we used in rollout (rollout_patch.diff) for triage. If rollback clears, we can schedule a canary re-rollout with tighter probes.

Marissa
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rollout_patch.diff (text)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:05:20 -0700
Subject: Update: actions completed and short-term mitigation (Acme)

Hi Lydia — quick customer update per your ask below. TL;DR: rollback applied, autoscaler restarted, short traffic shift completed, service validated.

What we did (completed):
- 08:41 PDT: initiated rollback to v20270328 for us-west-2 cluster A.
- 08:48 PDT: autoscaler process restarted and passed readiness probes.
- 08:50–09:00 PDT: Acme traffic routed to warm pools for 10 minutes while nodes stabilized; we saw tail latency return to baseline and failures drop to near-zero.
- We uploaded node traces and the incident snapshot to INC-20270410 (link below).

Proposed next steps:
1) Our team will prepare a short post-incident write-up within 72 hours (scope, root cause hypothesis, mitigation plan).
2) We propose a proactive canary rollout schedule with stricter health probes before broad rollouts.
3) As a gesture for the impact, we propose a preliminary 10% service credit for the minute-weighted affected window; we will finalize after your impact numbers.

I’ve attached a one-paragraph customer-ready update (customer_update_draft.txt) below — please let me know if you want different language or a 1:1 to walk through the technical details.

Again, sorry for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the RCA and a mitigations timeline.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Links: https://redwood.internal/ops/INC-20270410
Attachment: customer_update_draft.txt (text)
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>, ops@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Update: actions completed and short-term mitigation (Acme)

Thanks Diego — appreciate the rapid response and clear update. We’ll reconcile exact affected request counts and provide them by EOD. The 10% preliminary credit is acceptable pending those numbers. Please include a proposed date/time for the 1:1 RCA — we’d prefer sometime this week.

Also, for our internal risk review we’d like to get: 1) confirmation of the canary schedule you plan to use going forward, and 2) whether you will add circuit-breaker protections to prevent autoscaler stalls from impacting tail latency of reserved pools.

Lydia
(thread ends)
